patch.value: GET graph installs or activates pm-graph and bypasses edit permission

GET /api/projects/:projectId/pm/graph calls pmGraphExtensionGraphForProject, which calls ensureGraphExtension. The helper can install npm:pm-graph and activate it, so a safe-method request mutates project state. The pm router's permission middleware exempts GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, which also lets view-only collaborators trigger the mutation. This was found while tracing the complete CSRF boundary for pm-web-413z and must be repaired as a distinct route-semantics/authorization change.

GET /pm/graph is observational and never installs, activates, or otherwise mutates an extension; any explicit provisioning uses a CSRF-protected unsafe method and requires edit permission; view-only users can read the fallback graph without changing project state; real route tests prove command logs remain mutation-free on GET.
A state-changing GET can be triggered cross-origin and currently bypasses the edit-permission middleware by design.
Request GET /api/projects/:projectId/pm/graph for a project without active pm-graph; pmGraphExtensionGraphForProject calls ensureGraphExtension, which runs pm install and extension activate.
GET reads the installed graph when available or returns the fallback graph without mutation.
GET may install and activate pm-graph, including for view-only users.
Cross-origin or view-only callers can change a project's extension state through a nominally read-only endpoint.
